The manager and new hire should be able to name the role's decisions, interfaces, and success measures. Missing documentation found during onboarding is work to fix, not folklore the new hire is expected to memorize.

action.title: Performance review operating guide
action.body:
# Performance review operating guide

This guide is restricted to People and the CEO because it includes manager calibration mechanics. Individual reviews do not belong in Kival demo content.

## Cadence

Formal reviews happen twice per year. Managers maintain lightweight evidence continuously rather than reconstructing six months from memory.

## Calibration

Assess scope, outcomes, judgment, collaboration, and growth against role expectations. Do not normalize ratings to force a distribution. If expectations were unclear, fix the expectations before treating the ambiguity as a performance problem.

## Written record

The review should distinguish observed evidence, manager interpretation, and agreed next steps. Avoid speculative personality labels and unnecessary personal context.

action.title: Skill: Screen an inbound candidate
action.body:
# Skill: Screen an inbound candidate

**Purpose:** Prepare a consistent first-pass assessment against an approved role scorecard.

## Inputs

- role description and scorecard
- candidate-submitted material
- [[Recruiting process]]

## Procedure

1. Extract evidence relevant to the role's must-have criteria.
2. Mark missing evidence as unknown, not as a negative inference.
3. Identify concrete questions for the recruiter screen.
4. Flag logistics that need confirmation separately from capability assessment.
5. Produce a short recommendation with confidence and evidence links.

## Boundaries

Do not infer protected or sensitive personal attributes. Do not search for unrelated personal information. The recruiter owns the decision to progress a candidate and checks the source material before using the draft.

action.title: Skill: Prepare an offer packet
action.body:
# Skill: Prepare an offer packet

**Purpose:** Assemble the internal facts needed for an approved offer without letting compensation or role details drift between systems.

## Procedure

1. Confirm approved role, level, manager, location, and start-date range.
2. Confirm the compensation decision from the authorized source; never estimate missing numbers.
3. Summarize candidate evidence relevant to the final level decision.
4. List approvals still required.
5. Prepare candidate-facing copy only after the internal facts are confirmed.

## Boundary

An agent may prepare the packet, but it may not negotiate, promise terms, or invent compensation data. People owns the final offer and the authoritative employment documents.

action.title: 2026 marketing strategy
action.body:
# 2026 marketing strategy

ACME should be known for making complex commerce infrastructure operable, not for adding another layer of dashboards and slogans.

## Ideal customer

Product and engineering teams at growing merchants that have outgrown ad-hoc integrations but do not want a large enterprise platform migration.

## Motions

1. Product-led proof: technical content, examples, migration guides, and credible benchmarks.
2. Launch moments: concentrated narratives around meaningful product improvements.
3. Paid acquisition: narrowly targeted experiments that can be tied to qualified merchant intent.
4. Partnerships: co-marketing only where the partner reaches the same buyer with complementary value.

## What we will not do

Buy broad awareness because impressions are cheap. A campaign that cannot explain who should act and why is not ready for spend.

action.title: Brand voice and writing guide
action.body:
# Brand voice and writing guide

ACME should sound competent, calm, and specific.

## Prefer

- concrete claims over superlatives
- short explanations of trade-offs
- examples that show how the product behaves
- plain language for operationally complex ideas

## Avoid

- “revolutionary,” “game-changing,” and unsupported category claims
- pretending every feature is an industry first
- fear-based security messaging
- anthropomorphizing agents as if they independently own decisions

## Product naming

Use product and capability names consistently. When a term becomes overloaded, fix the glossary or messaging source rather than teaching every writer a private exception.

For current positioning, see [[Messaging architecture]].

action.title: Messaging architecture
action.body:
# Messaging architecture

## Company promise

ACME helps growing merchants run critical commerce workflows without turning their infrastructure into a black box.

## Pillars

### Operable by default

Teams can understand ownership, failure modes, and recovery paths.

### Evolves without surprise

Compatibility and migration are treated as product concerns, not cleanup work.

### Works with human and agent workflows

Knowledge, procedures, and constraints are explicit enough to be reused by both people and authorized agents.

## Evidence rule

Every external proof point should map to a real product behavior, customer result, benchmark, or documented practice. If evidence is weak, weaken the claim rather than decorating it.

action.title: Q3 content and campaign plan
action.body:
# Q3 content and campaign plan

The quarter is organized around three themes rather than a daily publishing quota.

## August — reliability proof

Technical article on asynchronous webhook delivery, incident-learning process, and migration safety.

## September — platform launch

Launch narrative, customer examples, product walkthrough, partner enablement, and targeted paid support.

## October — migration confidence

API v2 migration guide, implementation examples, and merchant engineering interview.

## Distribution

Each piece has one primary audience and one primary channel. Repurposing is welcome when the format still fits; we will not turn every article into ten low-value fragments to satisfy a calendar.

action.title: Paid acquisition operating model
action.body:
# Paid acquisition operating model

Paid acquisition is an experiment system, not a standing budget entitlement.

## Current channels

- Search: high-intent integration and migration terms.
- LinkedIn: narrow account/role tests around launch moments only.
- Retargeting: low spend, capped frequency.

## Guardrails

Every campaign needs a named hypothesis, audience, landing page, conversion event, stop condition, and owner. We do not optimize to click-through rate when qualified activation is the objective.

## Claims and privacy

Do not use customer names, security claims, or comparative claims without an approved source. Tracking additions that materially change data collection go through the normal privacy/security review before launch.

See [[Growth experiment scorecard]] for how experiments are evaluated.

action.title: Growth experiment scorecard
action.body:
# Growth experiment scorecard

Every paid or lifecycle experiment closes with the same questions.

- What audience and problem did we target?
- What changed relative to control or baseline?
- Did qualified activation improve, not just top-of-funnel volume?
- What did the experiment cost in spend and team attention?
- What would make us repeat, scale, modify, or stop it?

## Q3 thresholds

A paid channel is considered promising when the cohort shows acceptable activation quality and a modeled payback below 12 months at realistic conversion assumptions. We do not scale from a handful of conversions without checking cohort quality.

Negative results are durable knowledge when the hypothesis and setup are documented well enough not to rerun the same idea six weeks later.

action.title: Campaign: Northstar search experiment
action.body:
# Campaign: Northstar search experiment

**Owner:** Kate  
**Status:** running  
**Window:** 18 August – 15 September 2026

## Hypothesis

Merchants actively searching for webhook reliability and API migration guidance are more likely to activate than broad “commerce platform” traffic.

## Setup

Three tightly scoped ad groups point to technical landing pages. Spend is capped until at least 20 qualified activations or the stop-loss threshold is reached.

## Early signal

Click volume is lower than the previous broad campaign, but qualified demo-to-activation rate is materially higher. No budget increase until the first cohort reaches day-14 product usage.

## Decision

Keep the narrow intent terms. Pause the generic “commerce API” group if it remains below the activation threshold after another week.

action.title: September launch landing-page brief
action.body:
# September launch landing-page brief

The page has one job: help a technically credible buyer understand what changed, why it matters operationally, and whether the launch applies to their environment.

## Structure

1. Problem in buyer language.
2. New capability and concrete behavior.
3. Evidence: latency/reliability or workflow improvement where we have it.
4. Migration/adoption path.
5. Call to action for the right audience.

## Review

Product validates behavior. Engineering validates technical claims. Marketing owns clarity and conversion. Security reviews only claims or tracking changes that enter its scope.

Do not add logos, metrics, or “trusted by” language without a source that supports the exact statement.

action.title: Skill: Draft a campaign brief
action.body:
# Skill: Draft a campaign brief

**Purpose:** Turn an approved marketing objective into a reviewable campaign hypothesis before creative or spend starts.

## Inputs

- [[2026 marketing strategy]]
- target audience evidence
- product/launch source material
- channel constraints

## Output

State audience, problem, promise, evidence, channel, conversion event, budget boundary, stop condition, and owner.

## Agent boundary

An agent may synthesize research and draft variants. It must preserve uncertainty, cite the source behind factual claims, and must not turn an internal aspiration into an external fact.

action.title: Skill: Review an advertisement before launch
action.body:
# Skill: Review an advertisement before launch

**Purpose:** Catch avoidable claim, targeting, measurement, and brand problems before spend begins.

## Checklist

1. Is the audience specific enough to explain why this message should work?
2. Does every factual or comparative claim have a source?
3. Does the destination match the promise in the ad?
4. Is the conversion event meaningful for the hypothesis?
5. Are tracking and audience data uses already approved?
6. Is there a stop condition and accountable owner?
7. Does the copy match [[Brand voice and writing guide]]?

An agent can perform the first review pass. Judy or Kate approves the final ad and any material claim changes.

action.title: September platform launch plan

**Launch owner:** Grace

Track the final gate in [[Launch readiness checklist]] and decisions in commentary rather than creating parallel launch spreadsheets.

action.title: September launch messaging
action.body:
# September launch messaging

## Primary message

ACME's new platform release makes high-volume integration workflows more predictable under load and easier to operate when dependencies fail.

## Supporting proof

Use measured behavior and documented workflow improvements. Do not claim “zero downtime,” “self-healing,” or universal performance gains.

## Audiences

- Engineering leaders: operational predictability and migration safety.
- Product leaders: fewer integration failures interrupting merchant workflows.
- Existing customers: what changes, what does not, and what they need to do.

## Internal note

The launch should not imply that agents independently operate production. Agent-assisted workflows remain bounded by approval and ownership policies.

action.title: Partnership strategy
action.body:
# Partnership strategy

Partnerships should create distribution or product leverage that ACME cannot get efficiently by acting alone.

## Priority partner types

1. Commerce implementation partners with technically credible delivery teams.
2. Platforms whose merchants already need ACME integrations.
3. Technology partners where joint workflows remove material setup friction.

## Qualification

A partner needs a clear shared customer, an owner on both sides, and a plausible repeatable motion. Logo swaps without a customer path are not a partnership strategy.

## Operating model

Leo owns partner development. Grace owns product commitments. Marketing reviews co-marketing. Security joins when integration or data access materially changes risk.

action.title: September launch partner enablement
action.body:
# September launch partner enablement

This packet prepares integration partners for the September platform launch without asking them to decode internal engineering material.

## Partners need

- what changes for new integrations
- what remains compatible

- troubleshooting path
- customer-facing language they may reuse

## Internal owners

Grace owns product accuracy. Leo owns distribution and partner questions. Judy owns reusable external language. Engineering answers technical exceptions but does not become the default partner support queue.

Partner-specific commercial details do not belong in this packet.

action.title: Launch retrospective template
action.body:
# Launch retrospective template

Run this two weeks after a material launch, after initial usage data is available.

## Questions

- Did the intended audience understand the change?
- Did adoption match the rollout assumptions?
- Which support or reliability issues were predictable?
- Which campaign or partner motions produced qualified usage?
- What should become durable product, marketing, engineering, or partnership knowledge?
- Which repeated launch task should become or update a skill?

The retrospective should produce changes to source documents, not merely a meeting transcript.

action.title: Skill: Prepare a partner briefing
action.body:
# Skill: Prepare a partner briefing

**Purpose:** Produce a partner-facing technical/business brief from approved source material.

## Procedure

1. Identify the shared customer workflow.
2. State what the partner needs to know and do.
3. Separate public/approved claims from internal assumptions.
4. List product or technical dependencies with named ACME owners.
5. Remove internal commercial notes and unrelated restricted context.
6. Flag any unresolved commitment instead of phrasing it as decided.

Leo reviews the final packet. Product validates product commitments; Marketing validates reusable external copy.

action.title: Skill: Run a launch readiness review
action.body:
# Skill: Run a launch readiness review

**Purpose:** Turn the launch checklist and current source documents into a decision-ready go/no-go review.

## Procedure

1. Read [[Launch readiness checklist]].
2. For each open item, identify owner, evidence, and acceptance condition.
3. Separate launch blockers from follow-up work.
4. Highlight cross-functional inconsistencies: dates, claims, rollout assumptions, or support ownership.
5. Produce a concise list of decisions required before the gate.

An agent may prepare the review, but Grace owns the go/no-go decision. A missing signal stays missing; do not infer readiness from silence.

action.title: Information access model
action.body:
# Information access model

ACME uses functional groups and explicit object grants rather than assuming every workspace member should see every object.

## Baseline

Company handbook, directory, onboarding, and broadly useful policy material are readable by Everyone. Functional working material is normally editable by its owning group and only shared outward when another function needs it.

## Restricted by default

- candidate pipeline and assessment material — People plus the named hiring leads
- performance/calibration guidance — People and the CEO
- partner negotiation pipeline — Partnerships, Product owner, and CEO
- detailed growth experiments before publication — Marketing, relevant Product owners, and CEO
- security-sensitive operating material — Security plus the engineering/leadership roles that need it

## Cross-functional work

Launch objects deliberately combine Product and Marketing edit access with Engineering and Partnerships visibility. The access boundary follows the work, not the org chart.

## Agents

An agent inherits the authority of the identity and tool context under which it runs. A skill does not widen access. If a source object is outside that authority, the correct behavior is to surface the missing context rather than attempt to reconstruct it from unrelated material.
The People boundary is right. Hiring managers should get access to the role-specific hiring object, not to the entire recruiting or performance area just because they manage people.
Exactly. The useful default is narrow source access plus explicit cross-functional grants where the work actually requires them.
